name: Audit hours of service and ELD logs
summary: Compliance specialists work through each hours-of-service exception: a driving or on-duty limit broken, driving with no driver logged in, an edit or an uncertified day, or a paper log that does not match its receipts. They check the log against dispatch, fuel, toll and border records, get the driver to accept or explain, record the violation and the remedial action the regulation requires, and pass repeat cases to a safety manager. Paper logs, still common until the ELD mandate of June 2021, take days to arrive and must be scanned and keyed before they can be audited; electronic exceptions pile up in a queue and drivers on the road answer slowly.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees with about 1,210 company drivers and 380 owner-operators whose logs it must monitor.
baseline.notes: About 1,500 exceptions a month, roughly one per driver per month. About 35% of exceptions over the period came from paper logs (most before mid-2021); among ELD exceptions about 30% are unidentified driving, 22% edits or uncertified days, 33% limit violations, 4% malfunctions and 11% false alarms.

trigger: The ELD platform flags an exception, or a paper log arrives and the log audit tool flags a day.
end_state: The exception is cleared and filed, or a confirmed violation and its remedial action are recorded and passed to driver performance.

volume.seasonality: Higher in the autumn LTL peak and in winter, when weather delays push drivers against their limits; a burst of unidentified driving and edit exceptions followed each fleet's switch to certified ELDs in 2020-2021.

evidence.note: Organisation process map volume; Transport Canada estimates 5% to 10% of drivers routinely exceed limits, and unidentified driving and edits add to violations.

roles.title: Compliance specialist (hours of service and driver files)

evidence.note: About half of the 12-person team; the rest build driver files and track renewals. Author's estimate.
Scanning and keying paper logs at terminals, mostly before mid-2021. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.
Driver managers and linehaul supervisors discuss violations with drivers. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.
Repeat and serious violations only. Author's estimate.
Drivers' time to forward logs and respond to edits; stands in for drivers of every division and owner-operators. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.

systems.name: Electronic logging devices and telematics platform
Document imaging for bills of lading and delivery receipts
Transportation management system (LTL and truckload operations, billing, rating)
Fleet maintenance management system (work orders, PM schedules, parts)
Email, phone system and contact centre software
Safety management system (driver files, collisions, roadside inspections)

steps.name: Collect log data and flag exceptions
steps.description: For drivers with electronic logs, the ELD and telematics platform checks each day's record against the daily and cycle limits and raises exceptions for violations, unidentified driving, edits and uncertified days. For drivers still on paper logs, the case starts when the driver's log sheets come in.

next.condition: driver uses an ELD or electronic recorder

evidence.note: ELD provisions in force June 2021; before then many drivers used paper or unmandated electronic recorders. The 35% paper share is an average over 2019-2022 and is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Driver forwards paper logs and receipts
steps.description: The driver drops the week's log sheets, fuel receipts, toll and border receipts and bills of lading in the terminal drop box or mails them in. The rules allow up to 20 days after each day's record.

control.basis: Hours of Service Regulations s.85(1) and s.85(3)

evidence.note: Drivers forward records within 20 days; carriers deposit them at the principal place of business within 30 days.

steps.name: Scan and key paper logs
steps.description: A terminal service clerk sorts the log package, scans the sheets and receipts to the imaging system and keys duty status changes into the log audit tool, which flags the day that breaks a limit or does not match the receipts. One flagged exception usually means keying a week of logs.

error.defect_description: A duty status change keyed at the wrong time.

evidence.note: Carriers estimate about 3.5 minutes of clerical time to file each paper daily log; the number of logs keyed per exception is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Audit paper log against supporting documents
steps.description: The compliance specialist opens the flagged log and compares the recorded times and places with fuel receipts, tolls, border crossing times, bills of lading and GPS trip records, looking for driving shown as off duty or a second set of logs. The specialist confirms the violation or clears the flag.

error.defect_description: Falsified time missed because a receipt was not compared.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations s.87: carrier must monitor each driver's compliance and take and record remedial action

evidence.note: Carriers verify records against supporting documents such as bills of lading, payroll, fuel receipts and trip records; auditors check the same.

steps.name: Triage ELD exception
steps.description: The compliance specialist works through the exception queue in the ELD platform, opens each item and classifies it as unidentified driving, an edit or uncertified day, a limit violation, a device malfunction or a false alarm such as a yard move.

evidence.note: Exception mix is the author's estimate; categories follow the regulation and industry guidance.

steps.name: Investigate unidentified driving
steps.description: The compliance specialist matches the unit and time of the unidentified driving with dispatch records, yard and shop work orders and gate logs to find who was driving. Technicians' road tests and yard moves cannot be given to a driver.

next.condition: shop, yard or other non-driver movement

evidence.note: Carriers review the unidentified driver account and move time only to the driver who drove; technicians' test drives stay unassigned with a note.

steps.name: Propose reassignment to the driver's log
steps.description: The compliance specialist sends the unidentified segment to the identified driver's log through the ELD platform with a note explaining the evidence.

evidence.note: Drivers may refuse unassigned time.

steps.name: Ask driver to certify or explain an edit
steps.description: For uncertified days or edits without an adequate reason, the compliance specialist messages the driver through the ELD to certify the day or annotate the edit, and copies the driver manager when the driver is on the road.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Driver accepts edit or certifies log
steps.description: The driver reviews the proposed edit or uncertified day on the ELD tablet at the next stop and accepts, rejects with a comment or certifies it.

next.condition: rejected or no response after reminders

evidence.note: Drivers may refuse unassigned time; response rates are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Annotate unidentified driving record
steps.description: The compliance specialist annotates the unidentified segment with the reason (technician road test, yard move, tow) and leaves it in the unidentified driver account, which inspectors may ask to see.

control.basis: Hours of Service Regulations s.78.1 and s.99(1)(b)

evidence.note: Distinct account for unidentified driving time, produced on request.

steps.name: Verify limit violation against supporting documents
steps.description: The compliance specialist checks a flagged driving, on-duty or cycle violation against dispatch times, fuel and toll records and customs crossing times, and checks for allowed exceptions such as adverse driving conditions or deferred off-duty time.

error.defect_description: A real violation cleared as an allowed exception.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations s.87: carrier must monitor each driver's compliance and take and record remedial action

evidence.note: Limits and allowed deferral from the regulation; 5% to 10% of drivers routinely exceed limits (Transport Canada estimate).

steps.name: Notify driver manager of the violation
steps.description: The compliance specialist emails the driver manager or linehaul supervisor the violation, the evidence and the rule broken, and asks for the driver's explanation within a week.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Driver manager reviews violation with the driver
steps.description: The driver manager calls or meets the driver, hears the reason (customer delays, traffic, a planning error by dispatch), reminds them of the rule and records the explanation and the driver's acknowledgement.

evidence.note: Driver managers reach drivers between trips; author's estimate.

steps.name: Record violation and remedial action
steps.description: The compliance specialist re-keys the violation, the explanation and the remedial action (warning, coaching, load planning change) from the ELD platform and email into the driver's record in the safety system, with the dates as the regulation requires.

error.defect_description: Violation recorded against the wrong driver or date.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations s.87: carrier must monitor each driver's compliance and take and record remedial action

next.condition: repeat or serious violation (falsification, several in 30 days)

evidence.note: Remedial action and the dates of non-compliance must be recorded.

steps.name: Safety manager reviews repeat or serious violation
steps.description: The regional safety manager reads the driver's violation history, the evidence and the explanation and decides between retraining, a written warning, suspension or, for falsified logs, termination, in line with the progressive discipline policy and any collective agreement.

control.basis: Progressive discipline policy and collective agreement

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft discipline notice or coaching referral
steps.description: The safety manager writes the discipline notice or the referral to a trainer for an hours-of-service refresher and sends it to the driver manager and, for unionised drivers, labour relations.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Send violation to driver performance records
steps.description: The compliance specialist links the violation to the driver's safety performance record so it counts in coaching decisions and monthly reporting, files the supporting documents and closes the exception.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Close exception and file records
steps.description: The compliance specialist closes the exception with a resolution code and makes sure the record and supporting documents are kept for at least six months.

evidence.note: Records and supporting documents kept at least 6 months.

steps.name: Log ELD malfunction and open IT ticket
steps.description: The compliance specialist records the malfunction in the register, tells the driver to keep paper logs until the device is fixed, and opens a service desk ticket to repair or replace the device within 14 days.

evidence.note: Malfunctioning ELD repaired or replaced within 14 days.

steps.name: Request missing supporting documents
steps.description: The compliance specialist asks the terminal, the fuel card portal or the driver for the missing fuel receipt, toll record or bill of lading needed to confirm the times in the log.

evidence.note: Supporting documents named in the regulation; delays are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Falsified paper log
exceptions.description: Fuel or border receipts show driving while the log shows off duty; the case goes to the safety manager for discipline.

exceptions.name: Driver rejects reassigned time
exceptions.description: The driver refuses unidentified time the evidence points to them; the driver manager resolves it with the driver.

exceptions.name: Missing supporting documents
exceptions.description: A fuel receipt or bill of lading is needed to confirm the times and has to be requested.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from exception flagged (or paper log day) to closure
benchmarks.population: Hours-of-service exceptions at a mid-size Canadian carrier, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Paper logs may arrive up to 20 days after the day logged; ELD exceptions close in days when the driver responds. Levels are the author's estimate.

benchmarks.population: Canadian federally regulated carriers (Transport Canada regulatory impact analysis, 2019)
Canadian commercial vehicle drivers (Transport Canada estimate, 2019)

pain_points.description: Paper logs arrive up to 20 days late and each flagged exception means scanning and keying a week of sheets before anyone can audit it.

evidence.note: 20-day forwarding rule and 3.5 minutes per log.

pain_points.description: Unidentified driving from yard moves, shop road tests and forgotten logins fills the queue and must be traced by hand through dispatch and work orders.

evidence.note: Causes of unassigned time described by the Alberta Motor Transport Association.

pain_points.description: Drivers on the road answer edit requests and violation calls slowly, so exceptions sit open for days.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Violations are re-keyed from the ELD platform into the safety system, so driver records and reports lag.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313)
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: s.12-14: 13 h driving and 14 h on duty per day, 10 h off duty per day with 8 consecutive; s.26-27 cycle 1 of 70 h in 7 days and cycle 2 of 120 h in 14 days; s.85: drivers forward records of duty status within 20 days, carriers deposit them at the principal place of business within 30 days and keep them at least 6 months; s.86 bans duplicate or inaccurate records and ELD tampering; s.87: the motor carrier shall monitor each driver's compliance and on finding non-compliance take immediate remedial action and record the dates and actions; s.78.1 and s.99(1)(b): a distinct account for driving time of an unidentified driver, produced on request; s.78(5): repair or replace a malfunctioning ELD within 14 days; s.91 out-of-service declarations.

sources.title: Regulations Amending the Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (Electronic Logging Devices and Other Amendments), SOR/2019-165
sources.supports: ELD provisions in force on the second anniversary of publication (June 2021); 157,424 federally regulated CMVs need daily logs, 87,849 operate into the US; carriers estimate clerical staff take about 3.5 minutes to file each paper daily log; 4.5 minutes of driver time saved per record; Transport Canada estimates 5% to 10% of drivers routinely exceed HOS limits; 2.81% of inspections end in an HOS out-of-service order; about 9,400 HOS convictions a year, 48% for failing to maintain or produce a log; carriers verify records against supporting documents such as bills of lading, payroll, fuel receipts and trip records.

sources.title: Unassigned and Unidentified: Compliance considerations for Canadian ELDs
sources.supports: Driving without a logged-in driver goes to the ELD's unidentified driver account; the carrier reviews it and moves time only to the driver who actually drove; drivers may refuse unassigned time; technicians' test drives stay in the account with a note; causes include forgotten logins and misuse of yard move and personal conveyance settings; more than 30 minutes of unassigned driving triggers a malfunction code.

sources.title: Facility audits and new carrier compliance reviews
sources.supports: Facility auditors request driver file records and hours-of-service records with documentation that supports the reported hours, such as payroll records, gate tickets and fuel receipts; results can change the safety rating, add conditions or bring administrative penalties.

assumptions: Paper-log share of 35% is an average over 2019-2022: higher in 2019-2020, near zero for long-haul drivers after June 2021. Drivers within 160 km of home terminal (most pickup and delivery drivers) are exempt from daily logs and are outside this process.
The role tl-driver-longhaul stands in for drivers of every division and owner-operators' drivers; linehaul supervisors play the driver manager's part for LTL linehaul drivers.
Owner-operators' drivers' logs are audited by the carrier in the same way as company drivers'.
Compliance specialists work office hours; waits include nights and weekends.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's.
